description:
Redwood Inference is expanding enterprise security posture for Hosted, Dedicated, and (especially) Private deployments. This project standardizes the audit log event schema and reaches 100% coverage for sensitive actions across the platform so customers (and internal security/compliance) can reliably: (1) detect and investigate suspicious behavior, (2) satisfy SOC 2/ISO-aligned controls, and (3) export events to SIEMs with consistent semantics.

Goals
- Define a single canonical audit event schema (versioned) with required fields, consistent actor/target semantics, and explicit event taxonomy.
- Achieve 100% coverage for “sensitive actions” across API, Console/admin, control plane, routing/policy changes, RBAC changes, credential lifecycle, data retention/config, Private install/upgrade operations, and audit log export configuration.
- Provide a compatibility strategy (schema versioning + migration/normalization) so customers can consume logs across releases without breaking.
- Add enforcement and verification: build-time linting for event emission, runtime/telemetry-based coverage dashboards, and regression tests.
- Improve operability: runbooks for audit pipeline outages, backfill strategy, retention/redaction rules, and SIEM export guidance.

Scope
- In-scope systems: API Gateway, Control Plane services (tenant/config/policy/RBAC), Console backend/admin actions, Private installer/upgrade tooling, audit-log-exporter, observability ingestion, and data residency/retention configuration surfaces.
- In-scope outputs: Confluence standards + ADRs, implementation PRs, Linear project plan, Slack coordination, customer-facing support artifacts (Jira), and sales/security review collateral (Gmail/Fireflies/HubSpot).
- Out-of-scope: building a full customer-facing “audit log UI” beyond basic viewing/export configuration; new compliance certifications (this project supports them but is not itself the audit).

Key stakeholders / owners
- Product: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance), Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments), Marissa Cole / Paula Mendes (Console & Rollouts dependencies).
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin (exec owner for engineering delivery), Kevin Osei (audit log export + SIEM), Hanae Suzuki (supporting security eng).
- Platform/Engineering: Ethan Park (control plane), Priya Natarajan (platform org sponsor), Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (telemetry), Allison Grant (observability standards), Neha Kapoor / Sean Gallagher (SRE for reliability + incident response).
- GRC: Olga Petrov (control mapping, evidence expectations).

Timeline (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): inventory current events, define “sensitive actions” list, gap analysis by service.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): schema design + ADRs + reference implementation library; define versioning/backcompat policy.
- Phase 2 (4–8 weeks): roll out instrumentation service-by-service; add CI enforcement + tests.
- Phase 3 (2–4 weeks): coverage verification (dashboards + sampling), operational runbooks, customer export guidance, and launch comms.

Constraints / non-functional requirements
- Minimize PII: explicitly classify fields, enforce redaction/hashing rules, and avoid logging secrets.
- Cardinality control: constrain free-form strings, enumerate action types, and cap dimensions.
- Multi-deployment consistency: Hosted/Dedicated/Private must emit equivalent events for equivalent actions.
- Reliability: audit pipeline must be resilient (buffering/retry), with clear failure modes and on-call guidance.

Deliverables
- Canonical schema v1 (JSON schema + field dictionary) + event taxonomy for sensitive actions.
- Implementation library + service integration checklist.
- Coverage dashboard and “missing events” alerts.
- SIEM export format guidance + customer-facing security FAQ updates.
- Evidence mapping notes for SOC2/ISO controls and audit readiness.

files.description: Canonical audit event schema v1: required fields, optional extensions, actor/target/resource model, correlation IDs, tenancy fields, schema versioning, and examples for key event types.
Enumerated taxonomy of sensitive actions (RBAC changes, key lifecycle, policy/routing changes, retention settings, Private upgrade actions, etc.) mapped to event_type names and required fields.
Definition of “100% coverage”: what counts as sensitive, where events must be emitted, acceptance criteria, sampling/verification strategy, and known exclusions process.
Schema versioning policy (v1/v1.1), deprecation windows, field evolution rules, normalization guidance for exporters, and customer communication plan for breaking changes.
Data classification for audit fields, PII/secret handling rules, hashing/redaction patterns, and review checklist to prevent sensitive payload logging.
GRC-facing mapping of audit logging capabilities to SOC 2/ISO-aligned controls; evidence expectations, screenshots/queries to collect, and ownership.
Engineering standard for emitting audit events: naming conventions, required context, correlation/trace IDs, failure handling (best-effort vs guaranteed), and cardinality constraints.
ADR documenting the chosen schema structure, event taxonomy approach, and trade-offs (flattened vs nested fields, extensibility, SIEM compatibility, multi-deploy parity).
ADR covering delivery semantics (at-least-once vs best-effort), buffering, retry strategy, and how services behave during audit pipeline outages.
SRE runbook for audit log ingestion/export failures: detection signals, dashboards, mitigation steps, backfill guidance, and customer comms templates.
Runbook for responding to coverage regressions (new endpoints missing events): triage steps, ownership routing, and how to add enforcement tests.
Process for requesting/approving exceptions to audit logging coverage (temporary waivers), including risk assessment and expiry requirements.
Working inventory of current audit events by service/endpoints, identified gaps for sensitive actions, and proposed owners per area.
Notes from cross-functional schema workshop: unresolved questions, field naming debates, SIEM requirements, and follow-ups.
Spreadsheet-style doc estimating event volume, high-cardinality fields, and recommended constraints/allow-lists.
Draft PRD for audit logging standardization: user personas (security teams), requirements, non-goals, and launch plan.
Checklist of Private installer/upgrade actions requiring audit events; mapping to event types and where to instrument in the installer.
Working list of Console admin workflows (RBAC edits, API key creation, export config) mapped to required audit events and UI/BE touchpoints.
Collected customer requirements for SIEM export formats (Splunk, Sentinel, Datadog), retention needs, and common field expectations.
Proposal for audit log pipeline SLOs (delivery latency, drop rate), alert thresholds, and error budget policy.
Core engineering ticket to define schema v1 + JSON Schema artifact, including review checklist and example events.
PM ticket defining sensitive actions list, acceptance criteria for 100% coverage, and launch gating requirements.
Implement event_type enum registry + build-time lint rules to prevent unregistered event types and missing required fields.
Instrument control plane for RBAC changes and API key lifecycle events; add unit/integration tests.
Add audit events for sensitive gateway/admin endpoints (token issuance, key validation config, quota overrides), including actor identity and source IP.
Ensure Console backend emits audit events for admin actions (role edits, export config changes, retention settings), with consistent actor attribution.
Add audit events to private installer/upgrade flow: install, upgrade, rollback, config apply, and credential rotation.
Update exporter to tag schema_version, normalize legacy fields, and validate outgoing payloads against schema.
Build coverage dashboard: expected event types vs observed, per-service breakdown, and automated alerts for missing events.
Reliability improvements for audit event ingestion path (buffering, retry strategy, backpressure behavior) and failure-mode testing.
Standardize correlation IDs (request_id, trace_id, admin_action_id) across services to support investigations.
CI gate to ensure required fields present for audited codepaths; includes templates and examples for service owners.
Implement and validate redaction rules, ensure secrets never logged, document field-level retention and residency behavior.
Migration plan/ticket for legacy events: identify producers, implement normalization, and deprecate old fields.
End-to-end tests that execute sensitive actions and assert a correctly shaped audit event is produced (hosted + private mode fixtures).
SRE/observability ticket to create drop-rate and latency alerts for audit pipeline, with on-call routing and runbook links.
PM task to align docs and enablement for SIEM export (formats, field semantics, troubleshooting), including Security FAQ updates.
Add/validate exporter targets for common SIEMs (Splunk HEC, Sentinel), including auth, batching, and failure handling.
Console validation and safe workflows for configuring export destinations; prevent misconfigurations and ensure audited changes.
Emit audit events for routing/policy changes (fallback rules, allow-lists), including diff summary and approver context.
Audit events for data residency/retention setting changes, capturing previous/new values and scope (tenant/project).
Finalize Confluence docs, runbooks, and internal enablement; verify links from dashboards/alerts and incident templates.
PR adding shared audit event library (structs + JSON schema validation), plus example producers and unit tests in the monorepo.
PR introducing a centralized event_type registry/enum and rejecting unknown types at build-time and/or runtime.
PR instrumenting RBAC CRUD endpoints to emit v1 audit events with actor identity, diff summaries, and correlation IDs.
PR adding audit events for API key creation/rotation/revocation, including secure redaction of key material.
PR adding audit events for gateway admin actions (quota overrides, key policy changes) and normalizing actor attribution from auth context.
PR emitting events when routing policies/fallback configurations are updated; includes diff generation and cardinality checks.
PR standardizing request_id/trace_id propagation and ensuring audit events include correlation fields across services.
PR adding end-to-end tests that perform sensitive actions and assert corresponding audit events are produced and validated.
PR introducing CI checks/lints for missing required fields and unregistered event types; includes developer guidance in repo docs.
PR adding audit events for retention/residency configuration changes with before/after summaries.
Exporter PR to include schema_version, validate outgoing payloads, and normalize legacy producers into v1 shape.
Exporter PR adding Splunk HEC target with batching, retry/backoff, and failure visibility metrics.
Exporter PR adding Azure Sentinel/Log Analytics export support and configuration examples for Private deployments.
Private installer PR to emit audit events for install/upgrade/rollback/config-apply actions and include operator identity where available.
PR adding dashboards/alerts for audit event ingestion latency and drop rate, plus links to the SRE runbook.
PR adding an SLO definition for audit log delivery (latency + error rate), with error budget alerts tuned for enterprise tiers.
Customer ticket: Private deployment customer reports missing RBAC change events; includes environment details, expected vs observed, investigation notes, and resolution plan.
Customer ticket: SIEM export contains inconsistent fields across event types; support collects samples, routes to Security Eng, and tracks fix rollout.

Internal ticket to grant Security/GRC access to new coverage dashboard and define least-privilege roles.
Internal ticket: initial alert thresholds too noisy; SRE tunes thresholds and updates runbook guidance.
Customer ticket capturing security questionnaire Q&A about audit schema fields, retention, residency, and export options; links to Confluence guidance.

Thread coordinating updates to Security FAQ / enablement materials and agreeing on externally communicable statements about audit logging behavior.
Transcript of customer security review call focusing on audit logging fields, retention, export targets (Splunk/Sentinel), and Private deployment parity; includes next steps.
Technical deep dive transcript with Solutions Engineering discussing Private logging architecture, buffering/retry, and customer SOC requirements; includes action items.

CRM company record (enterprise, Private) with notes emphasizing audit logging coverage, SIEM export, retention/residency constraints, and security review status; links to Fireflies and Gmail threads.
CRM record for regulated healthcare prospect evaluating Private; notes include audit log requirements, RBAC/SSO needs, and procurement blockers.
Mid-market customer using Dedicated; notes include request for normalized audit events and Splunk export; links to SUP ticket and exporter PR.

Thread tuning alert thresholds after initial rollout created noise; includes proposed changes and agreement to update runbook.
Thread discussing event_id generation (UUID vs ULID), dedupe keys, and customer guidance for SIEM duplicates.
Thread on implementing build-time enforcement: where to hook CI, how to keep dev experience reasonable, and exceptions mechanism.

Thread preparing for an enterprise security review: what docs to share, how to describe audit delivery semantics, and which roadmap items to avoid promising.

Thread coordinating response to a customer asking for proof of coverage; Support requests a coverage report screenshot and GRC-approved wording.
